steps.text: Sauté stew meat, onion, and celery in a large saucepan over medium-high heat until meat is browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Stir in carrots, then season with bouillon, parsley, and pepper. Stir in water and add egg noodles.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Beef Noodle Soup
raw_recipe.description: This delicious beef noodle soup recipe is always a hit. Stew meat, mixed vegetables and egg noodles are combined in beef broth base in this favorite.
raw_recipe.name: Beef Noodle Soup

recipeInstructions.text: Sauté stew meat, onion, and celery in a large saucepan over medium-high heat until meat is browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Stir in carrots, then season with bouillon, parsley, and pepper. Stir in water and add egg noodles.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 30 minutes.

review.reviewBody: Hey Brenda, this was a really good and totally comforting soup! The only major thing I changed was eliminating the water and beef boullion and using low salt beef broth. After browning my beef and vegies I put everything into my crock pot. For those who mentioned that the meat was tough, the slow cooker seemed to be the answer. I always add more seasonings (garlic and onion powder) and I boiled my egg noodles in a separate sauce pan and then added them to the slow cooker at the very end. Hubby Drew and kid Ash (Ty was at dance) went nuts over this! Thanks Brenda for a very quick and satisfying meal!

I used ground beef because it's what I had on hand. My husband loved this so much, he wanted more for dinner after having it for lunch today. Now that's a compliment. I scaled this down to 1.5 servings, so everything was cut back to a quarter of written. I did tweak this a little because that is how it is in my kitchen, but the adjustments were minor such as a light sprinkle of salt while the veggies were sweating it out in the pan, tossing a bay leaf in, a pinch of thyme, a dash of garlic powder, and some Kitchen Bouquet browning sauce which is made with carrots, onion, and celery so it has a similar profile to the base with the mirepoix beginnings of this soup. I do use a fairly heavy hand with black pepper so I likely added more than written. Since I let this simmer a while for flavor, I did have to add more broth (Better Than Bouillion and water) as it cooked. I put a few more noodles because I only had a little more in the bag and so I just tossed them it too. This is a keeper. Thanks for sharing as this is such a great base and easily customizable! My husband said it was the best.

EXCELLENT! I sprinkled flour on the meat after browning to thicken. Then I added 2 cans beef broth & 1 can of water w/ spices & cooked 25 mins in a pressure cooker. Then I added dry egg noodles (No Yolks) at the end, cooking until soft. Very flavorful & tender! Even my picky boys loved it, which hardly ever happens. One of my favorite recipes from this site!!

The children love chicken noodle soup, so I thought they might like this soup too, and they did.
I made some changes to use what was available in the fridge. I used bone in lamb pieces that I wrapped in a big piece of cheese clothe to make it easy to fish out of the soup to debone later. I put everything in the slow cooker except the noodles. I added 1 chopped clove of garlic and 1 bay leaf to make the broth more flavorful. I cooked on low for 8 hours. 
I deboned and shredded the lamb and put back with the noodles that I cooked separately on the stove and drained. I kept the soup in the slow cooker another 30 minutes, then added some chopped fresh parsley.

Yummo! We made a 1/2 batch, since I only had .5lb of leftover beef roast. I sauteed the veggies in garlic, then cooked them with yhechopped beef, 1 can condensed french onion soup, 3 cans water, and 2 beef buillion cubes. Fam LOVED it (which is saying a lot; my kiddos arent big soup eaters).

It was delicious and easy. Great flavor. I did add 1 can of beef broth because that's all I had. I browned the beef and veggies than put it in a crock pot. I cooked the noodles separate then added them about 15 minutes before we were ready to eat.

Total comfort food! I used dry, no yolk dumpling noodles, 5 c. Emeril's Organic Beef Stock + 1 c. of his Veg. Stock in place of bouillon & water. Didn't have stewing beef, so I substituted some left over Roast Beef that I cooked in my crock pot & added the last 30 min. with the noodles. Hubby & I ate this for dinner with a grilled cheese on sourdough & tomatoes with left overs for lunch! Yum Yum! A keeper for sure.

I sauteed 3 cloves of garlic with the beef, onion, celery and carrots. Added 1 can beef broth, 1 can diced tomatoes with juice, a few dashes Worcestershire, a few shakes of basil, the parsley, black pepper to taste, a bay leaf, 8 cups water, 3 Tbsp. Beef Bullion Granules and a splash of Balsamic Vinegar. Also threw in a bag of sliced button mushrooms and a bunch of green beans. Couldn't find the frozen egg noodles, so decided to go with frozen 4 Cheese Tortellini instead. Added a handful of Parm. WONDERFUL SOUP!

I found it to be in need of some help. First the recipe was too salty. I added a clove of minced garlic, substituted the water with beef broth, plus one teaspoon beef base, one can mushrooms, one teaspoon Herb de Provence, 1/4 cup Marsala wine, and used dry egg noodles. I cooked the beef in the broth for 2 hours on simmer, after browning. I then finished the recipe. It turned out great.

The only thing I changed with this recipe as good as it was instead of the bullion granules I used better than bouillon added more water and used a whole package of egg noodles. I used two teaspoons of better than bouillon that added more flavor than the beef bouillon granules and less salt.

Good basic recipe, but not as tasty as expected. 
I added Italian spices, rosemary, thyme and extra coarse pepper to add flavor.
Fantastic, of course, being from New Orleans I added cayenne pepper and Tony Chachere seasoning. Salt to taste when finished. As we say here: Laissez Les Bons Tems Roulet'!
I absolutely loved this soup and the simplicity of it. The only thing I changed was using dry noodles. This is going to be my go to recipe
This was delicious! After reading the reviews I decided to add some salt and some of my favorite seasonings to taste, and I’d recommend the same.
This is a fantastic recipe. I added a little garlic powder and I did swap the bullion for broth. Otherwise, I made no changes.
i used beef broth and seasoned each ingredient group with s&P and added a bay leaf for the final 25 minutes
I made this for my husband who was recuperating after a stay in hospital and needed to be tempted with a tasty, low-fat, easy -to-manage food and this was perfect!
Excellent. Used low sodium broth and dried egg noodles instead of frozen.

The recipe is great. So glad I made it. Kudos to the cook!
Like any recipe we can build on it, but I get really tired of people changing up recipes completely and then bragging and giving "themselves" 5 stars for their totally changed recipe. 
Or, changes are made and then the cook rates the original recipe poorly even though they changed it .
